description:
## Problem
VectorSearchQueryManager.get_query (benchbox/core/vector_search/queries.py) returns a variant, raises QuerySkippedError for a SKIP_QUERY rule, or else translates the DuckDB query with translate_sql_query. Since fork 30.35.0.4, DuckDB ARRAY_COSINE_SIMILARITY parses to a CosineSimilarity node, so the fallback now emits COSINE_SIMILARITY(a, b) instead of ARRAY_COSINE_SIMILARITY(a, b). The PR #4537 review found that BigQuery, SQLite, MySQL, Redshift, DataFusion and QuestDB have neither function, so those queries fail at execution instead of being skipped with a recorded reason. Trino has COSINE_SIMILARITY. This is not a regression: the old name did not exist on those engines either.

## Change
For each platform that reaches the translation fallback, decide from vendor documentation (cite the page) or an engine run: add a variant where the engine has an equivalent (for example BigQuery COSINE_DISTANCE or ML.DISTANCE), or a SKIP_QUERY rule with the reason in benchbox/sql_compat/rules/query_source/vector_search_variants.py.

## Decision gates
- G0: first confirm which platforms the CLI and platform manifest actually allow to run vector_search. If the fallback is unreachable for a platform, leave it out; if it is unreachable for all six, drop this item with that evidence.
- G1: where an engine has an equivalent function, the owner chooses a variant (needs a result-equivalence check) or a skip.

## Verification rubric
Pass only if: every reachable platform is either served by a variant with a cited function reference and an equivalence test, or raises QuerySkippedError with a reason in a test; no reachable platform receives a function its documentation lacks.

## Guardrails
- Variants and skips go through the sql_compat registry; no text replacement in benchbox/core.
- No live-cloud runs without owner approval; documentation evidence is enough for skips.
- Write work: linked worktree, pinned human identity, no agent attribution, changelog fragment, make pr-preflight, make pr-open, make pr-arm.
